topic: Proteus: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses — Plug In, Evolve, Measure

key_points: Open-source (MIT) research-preview framework for self-evolution of ANY agent harness; tagline 'Plug in. Evolve. Measure.'
Harness-agnostic: implement one small HarnessAdapter and your agent (minimal, llm, DeepSeek Harness, Pi, Aki, or your own) plugs into the same framework, sandbox, and measurement
Spans goal AND no-goal regimes with visible or hidden evaluators — no-goal unpressured evolution is a first-class mode
Ships a measurement instrument, not just a score: structural distance per surface, crystallization/swap test, and behavioural distance with a permutation test
Episode loop is four phases: observe → propose → act → reflect; evolved harness files cross episode boundaries with snapshotting and rollback
Core objects: HarnessAdapter, Surface, Disposition (removable action-preference perturbation), GoalConfig, Sandbox (Local or Docker)
v0.3.0 research preview, Python 3.10+, 57 GitHub stars, created 2026-08-17
A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents — 94 HN points, the canonical academic overview
Unified conceptual framework: System Inputs, Agent System, Environment, and Optimisers as the four feedback-loop components
Reviews self-evolving techniques targeting different agent-system components plus domain-specific strategies (biomedicine, programming, finance)
Dedicated discussion of evaluation, safety, and ethical considerations for self-evolving agentic systems
Frames the field as bridging static foundation-model capabilities with continuous lifelong adaptability
EvoHarnessRL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
Exposes Belief, Progress, and Experience (BPE) as policy-facing harness state; supervised harness fine-tuning + cost-aware GRPO
Reaches 96.9% success on ALFWorld with a Qwen3-8B LLM
Reveals two dynamics: harness annealing (training internalizes recurring harness-use patterns) and harness evolution (progress updates and experience consolidation refine the harness)
Treats external workspace and its usage policy as learnable rather than manually engineered
Cline achieved 88.8% SOTA on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via one-shot recursive self-improvement
Run cost $49.8 vs Fable 5's $552 — SOTA at less than a tenth of the price
A single prompt kicked off 17 hours of continuous coding-agent run with GPT-5.6-Sol as leader; ~1 billion tokens total (400M agent, 600M eval)
The model made its own PR — a first-of-its-kind hill climb that turned a good score into a SOTA score
Argues the bottleneck isn't models but the humans using them; weeks of human trace-reading work compressed into one prompt
Defines harness engineering: 'A coding agent is the model plus everything you build around it'
Agent = Model + Harness; a raw model is not an agent until a harness gives it state, tools, feedback loops, and constraints
Harness includes system prompts, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, skills, tools/MCP, sandbox, orchestration, hooks, and observability
Key claim: 'A decent model with a great harness beats a great model with a bad harness'
Viv Trivedy coined the term; frames most agent failures as configuration 'skill issues' rather than model-weight problems
SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills — Microsoft, 16.4K GitHub stars
First systematic controllable text-space optimizer for agent skills; a separate optimizer model turns scored rollouts into bounded add/delete/replace edits
An edit is accepted only when it strictly improves a held-out validation score; textual learning-rate budget + rejected-edit buffer for stability
Best or tied on all 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells across six benchmarks, seven target models, three execution harnesses
Beats human, one-shot LLM, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA, and EvoSkill per-cell competitors

stats.fact: Proteus is MIT-licensed, Python 3.10+, v0.3.0 research preview, with 57 GitHub stars and 7 forks as of 2026-08-27
Proteus demo run: an installed action preference (review_notes arm) shifted mean units built from 3.5 (neutral) to 13.0, with behavioural R = 3.075, p = 0.0150
Proteus's behavioural ruler independently reproduces research-run headline dynamics: arms separate at episode 1 (R = 1.63) and converge by episode 30 (R = 0.93)
EvoHarnessRL reaches 96.9% success on ALFWorld with a Qwen3-8B LLM by learning harness policies (Belief, Progress, Experience state)
Cline achieved 88.8% SOTA on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via one-shot recursive self-improvement at $49.8 — less than a tenth of Fable 5's $552 cost
Cline's SOTA run consumed ~1 billion tokens (400M by the coding agent, 600M by repeated eval runs) over 17 hours with GPT-5.6-Sol as leader model
SkillOpt is best or tied on all 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells across six benchmarks, seven target models, and three execution harnesses
SkillOpt has 16,417 GitHub stars and is described as the first systematic controllable text-space optimizer for agent skills
The self-evolving AI agents survey (arxiv 2508.07407) received 94 Hacker News points and abstracts the field via four components: System Inputs, Agent System, Environment, and Optimisers
Proteus roadmap names Hermes Agent as the first target harness to onboard, followed by SWE-agent, OpenClaw, Codex CLI, OpenHands, OpenCode, and Goose

angles: The 'harness is the new frontier' thesis: agent self-improvement is moving from model weights to the harness (prompts, memory, skills, tools, control loop) — Proteus is a ruler for that shift
Proteus's unique question vs other systems: not 'how do I raise a benchmark score' but 'what does a self-evolving harness actually DO, and does an initial condition leave a permanent mark?'
The measurement-first differentiator: structural distance, crystallization/swap test, and behavioural permutation test — most competitors only report task pass-rates
No-goal evolution as a first-class mode: unpressured self-evolution is a genuinely novel regime most harness-evolution systems hard-code away
Harness-agnostic onboarding: one HarnessAdapter plugs in any agent (DeepSeek Harness, Pi, Aki, your own) — versus competitors that only evolve their own primitives
The safety angle: self-editing agents write and run their own code, so Proteus runs real harnesses in a container whose filesystem holds the harness and nothing else (DockerSandbox with no egress)
Cost/efficiency contrast: Cline's $49.8 SOTA vs Fable's $552 shows recursive self-improvement is now cheap enough for individual developers
The 'bottleneck isn't models, it's humans' argument: weeks of human trace-reading compressed into a single prompt — a compelling narrative for practitioners
